outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Limitations of Tokenization and the Case for Raw Bytes
outline.description: This chapter introduces the fundamental problem addressed by the research: the inefficiencies and biases inherent in fixed-vocabulary tokenization (like BPE). It sets the stage for understanding why Byte Latent Transformers (BLT) are necessary, highlighting issues such as domain sensitivity, noise vulnerability, and the inability to capture orthographic nuances. It contrasts the historical reliance on tokenization with the computational challenges of byte-level modeling.
subtopics: The prevalence of tokenization in modern Large Language Models (LLMs)
Inherent biases of fixed-vocabulary tokenizers (domain sensitivity, multilingual inequity)
Shortcomings regarding noise robustness and orthographic knowledge
Historical barriers to byte-level training: Sequence length and computational cost
Why previous attempts failed at scale: The dominance of Feed-Forward Network costs over Attention costs
Introducing the core thesis: Dynamic compute allocation via patches

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: From Bytes to Patches – Strategies for Dynamic Grouping
outline.description: This chapter delves into the core mechanism of BLT: 'Patching'. It explores how raw bytes are grouped into variable-sized units called patches to optimize computation. Students will learn about different patching strategies, ranging from simple static rules to sophisticated entropy-based methods. The chapter emphasizes how these groupings allow the model to skip expensive computations for predictable data while focusing resources on complex regions.
subtopics: Defining Patches vs. Tokens: Variable vs. Fixed Vocabulary
Static Strided Patching: Pros, cons, and lack of context awareness
Whitespace/Simple Boundary Patching: Linguistic unit alignment
Entropy-Based Patching: Using a small language model to detect uncertainty
Mathematical formulation of patch boundaries (Global vs. Monotonic constraints)
Incremental Patching requirements for autoregressive generation

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Architectural Deep Dive – The Three-Part BLT System
outline.description: A technical breakdown of the Byte Latent Transformer architecture. This chapter explains how BLT integrates three distinct components: a lightweight local encoder, a powerful global latent transformer, and a local decoder. It details how information flows between raw bytes and latent patch representations, specifically focusing on the novel cross-attention mechanisms that bridge byte-level detail with patch-level semantics.
